# Setup

```{r}

library(GenomicRanges)
library(rtracklayer)
library(GenometriCorr)
library(tools)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)

# install.packages(c("future", "future.apply"))
library(future)
library(future.apply)

# Paths, chromosome accessions/lengths and parameters are kept in config.yaml.
config <- yaml::read_yaml("config.yaml")

sig_dir        <- config$correlation$paths$selective_signatures_dir
merged_cnv_dir <- config$correlation$paths$merged_cnv_calls_dir
merged_sig_dir <- config$correlation$paths$merged_selective_signatures_dir

# Threads to use
plan(multisession, workers = 8)
setwd(config$correlation$paths$working_dir)
```

```{r}
# Load unmerged per-sample selective signatures (used by the fragmentation
# sweep below to choose a merge distance).

all_files <- list.files(
  path = sig_dir,
  pattern = "\\.bed$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

not_consistently_selected <- all_files[
  !grepl("consistently", basename(all_files))
]

sample_names <- sub("_selective_signatures\\.bed$", "", basename(not_consistently_selected))

per_sample <- setNames(
  lapply(seq_along(not_consistently_selected), function(i) {
    gr <- import.bed(not_consistently_selected[i])
    gr$sample_id <- sample_names[i]   # reusable in plots, etc.
    gr
  }),
  sample_names
)
```

# Genometricorr


```{r}

library(GenomicRanges)
library(rtracklayer)
# specific library for arranging multiple plots

# ==============================================================================
# 1. Merge Function (Standard)
# ==============================================================================
merge_track <- function(gr, threshold) {
  mcols(gr) <- NULL
  # min.gapwidth = threshold + 1 mimics bedtools merge -d
  merged_gr <- GenomicRanges::reduce(gr, min.gapwidth = threshold + 1)
  return(merged_gr)
}

# ==============================================================================
# 2. Bulk Merge (Standard)
# ==============================================================================
merge_list_of_tracks <- function(gr_list, threshold) {
  lapply(gr_list, function(x) merge_track(x, threshold))
}

# ==============================================================================
# 3. Parameter Sweep Function (Optimized)
# ==============================================================================
analyze_fragmentation_thresholds <- function(gr_list, thresholds) {

  results_list <- vector("list", length(thresholds))
  message(paste("Starting sweep across", length(thresholds), "thresholds..."))

  for (i in seq_along(thresholds)) {
    thresh <- thresholds[i]

    # Calculate stats per sample for this threshold
    stats <- vapply(gr_list, function(gr) {
      merged <- merge_track(gr, thresh)

      n_intervals <- length(merged)
      # Calculate total genomic width in Megabases (Mb) for readability
      total_width_mb <- sum(width(merged)) / 1e6

      rm(merged) # Memory cleanup
      return(c(count = n_intervals, coverage = total_width_mb))
    }, FUN.VALUE = c(count = 0, coverage = 0))

    # Aggregate results
    results_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
      threshold = thresh,
      avg_intervals = mean(stats["count", ]),
      sd_intervals  = sd(stats["count", ]),
      avg_coverage  = mean(stats["coverage", ]),
      sd_coverage   = sd(stats["coverage", ])
    )

    if(i %% 5 == 0) message(paste("Processed threshold:", thresh))
    gc(verbose = FALSE)
  }

  do.call(rbind, results_list)
}

# ==============================================================================
# 4. Dual Plotting Function (Intervals + Coverage)
# ==============================================================================
#' Plots Count and Coverage side-by-side to identify the optimal window
plot_fragmentation_diagnostics <- function(stats_df) {

  # --- Plot 1: The Knee (Fragmentation) ---
  p1 <- ggplot(stats_df, aes(x = threshold, y = avg_intervals)) +
    geom_line(color = "#2980b9", size = 1) +
    geom_point(color = "#2980b9", size = 2) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = avg_intervals - sd_intervals,
                      ymax = avg_intervals + sd_intervals),
                  width = 0.1 * max(stats_df$threshold), alpha = 0.3) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = "Metric A: Fragmentation",
      subtitle = "Look for the 'Knee' (where drop stabilizes)",
      y = "Avg Interval Count",
      x = "Merge Distance (bp)"
    )

  # --- Plot 2: The Explosion (Over-merging) ---
  p2 <- ggplot(stats_df, aes(x = threshold, y = avg_coverage)) +
    geom_line(color = "#c0392b", size = 1) +
    geom_point(color = "#c0392b", size = 2) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = avg_coverage - sd_coverage,
                      ymax = avg_coverage + sd_coverage),
                  width = 0.1 * max(stats_df$threshold), alpha = 0.3) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = "Metric B: Total Genomic Footprint",
      subtitle = "Look for the 'Spike' (avoid large increases)",
      y = "Total Size (Mb)",
      x = "Merge Distance (bp)"
    )

  # Arrange side by side
  grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
}


```

```{r}
n_points <- 100
thresholds_linear <- as.integer(round(seq(
  from = 0,
  to   = 10000,
  length.out = n_points
)))

stats <- analyze_fragmentation_thresholds(per_sample, thresholds_linear)
plot_fragmentation_diagnostics(stats)
```

### Reload Merged Genome Tracks

Merged using:

``` bash
cut -f1-3 {} |
  sort -k1,1 -k2,2n |
  bedtools merge -d 10000 -i - |
  sort -k1,1 -k2,2n \
    > {/.}_merged_10kb_distance.bed
```

### Correlations between Genomic Tracks

```{r}
# Chromosome X (...0002.1) is excluded to preserve a valid permutation null
# (also filtered out from the Pool-HMM run). Accessions and lengths come from config.
chromosome_lengths <- unlist(config$correlation$chromosome_lengths)
included_chroms <- names(chromosome_lengths)
```

```{r}
calculate_pair_correlation <- function(query_gr, ref_gr, included_chroms, chromosome_lengths, permutations = 100) {


  # 2. Run GenometriCorrelation
  # We use awhole.only=TRUE to get a global correlation score
  res <- GenometriCorrelation(
    query = query_gr,
    reference = ref_gr,
    chromosomes.to.proceed = included_chroms,
    chromosomes.length = chromosome_lengths,
    awhole.only = TRUE,
    permut.number = permutations,
    keep.distributions = FALSE,
    showProgressBar = FALSE
  )

  # 3. Extract Results from the 'awhole' slot
  # The result is an S4 object, acting like a list.
  # We extract the ECDF correlation (a robust measure) and the Projection Test P-value.

  res_stats <- res[["awhole"]]

  print(res_stats)

  return(list(
    correlation = res_stats$relative.distances.ecdf.area.correlation,
    correlation.pval = res_stats$relative.distances.ecdf.deviation.area.p.value,
    correlation.pval.ks = res_stats$relative.distances.ks.p.value,
    jaccard = res_stats$jaccard.measure,
    jaccard.pval = res_stats$jaccard.measure.p.value
  ))
}
```

```{r}
run_batch_correlation_parallel <- function(track_list_1,
                                           track_list_2,
                                           included_chroms,
                                           chromosome_lengths,
                                           permutations = 100) {
  # 1. Create a grid of all index pairs to process
  # This "flattens" the nested loops so we can distribute work evenly
  combinations <- expand.grid(
    i = seq_along(track_list_1),
    j = seq_along(track_list_2),
    KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE
  )

  # Helper function (defined inside, so it ships to workers automatically)
  get_track_name <- function(gr, list_name, index) {
    if (!is.null(gr$sample_id))
      return(unique(gr$sample_id)[1])
    if (!is.null(names(list_name)))
      return(names(list_name)[index])
    return(paste0("Track_", index))
  }

  # 2. Run the calculation in parallel
  # future_lapply replaces the loop. It splits the work across available workers.
  results_list <- future_lapply(seq_len(nrow(combinations)), function(k) {
    # Get indices for this specific job
    i <- combinations$i[k]
    j <- combinations$j[k]

    t1 <- track_list_1[[i]]
    t2 <- track_list_2[[j]]

    name1 <- get_track_name(t1, track_list_1, i)
    name2 <- get_track_name(t2, track_list_2, j)

    # Run the external correlation function
    # Ensure 'calculate_pair_correlation' is loaded in your global environment
    metrics <- calculate_pair_correlation(t1, t2, included_chroms, chromosome_lengths, permutations = permutations)

    # Return the single row data frame
    return(
      data.frame(
        Track1 = name1,
        Track2 = name2,
        Correlation = metrics$correlation,
        P_value = metrics$correlation.pval,
        Jaccard = metrics$jaccard,
        Jaccard_pval = metrics$jaccard.pval,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    )

  }, future.seed = TRUE) # future.seed = TRUE ensures reproducibility if random numbers are used

  # 3. Combine all results into one data frame
  return(do.call(rbind, results_list))
}
```

```{r}
visualize_correlations <- function(corr_data,
                                   corr_col = "Correlation",
                                   pval_col = "p_value",
                                   title = "Lorem Ipsum",
                                   subtitle = "",
                                   title_x_axis = "x-axis",
                                   title_y_axis = "y-axis",
                                   title_colorscale = "Genometric\nCorrelation",
                                   infer_limits = FALSE,
                                   limit_min = -1,
                                   limit_max = 1) {
  # Determine limits
  if (infer_limits) {
    vals <- corr_data[[corr_col]]
    vals <- vals[is.finite(vals)]
    if (length(vals) == 0) {
      L <- 1
    } else {
      L <- max(abs(vals), na.rm = TRUE)
      if (L == 0)
        L <- 1e-6
    }
    lim <- c(-L, L)
  } else {
    lim <- c(limit_min, limit_max)
  }

  ggplot(corr_data, aes(x = Track1, y = Track2, fill = .data[[corr_col]])) +
    geom_tile(color = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = .data[[pval_col]]), color = "black", size = 3) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "blue",
      high = "red",
      mid = "white",
      midpoint = 0,
      limits = lim,
      space = "Lab",
      name = title_colorscale
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        size = 10
      ),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      panel.grid.major = element_blank()
    ) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x = title_x_axis,
      y = title_y_axis
    ) +
    coord_fixed()
}

```
